A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISP framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original LaMP experiments, computational measurements, ablations and larger-backbone evaluations, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds initialization comparisons, data-access controls and LongLaMP evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions generate a Text-to-LoRA anchor, initialize bridge C as the identity, freeze A, and optimize B and C using user history. The added training-input description and theoretical appendix document the retained procedure; they do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 adds LongLaMP product-review writing and abstract generation to the six retained LaMP tasks (Appendix C, Table 10). This substantially extends task requirements to long-form generation using extended user history. Larger-backbone LaMP evaluation already existed in v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds PiSSA and LoRA-GA as evaluated initialization comparators on LaMP-2, LaMP-3 and LaMP-7 (Table 4). This is a focused expansion; the main NP, RAG/PAG, Per-Pcs, PriME and OPPU comparator set remains.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled task-data access comparisons on LaMP-2/4: PRISP receives 50 task examples, while additional OPPU and RAG+PAG conditions omit task data (Table 9). Existing main splits, budgets, metrics and hyperparameters remain unchanged. Figure 9 switches from training-step summaries to layer-index results, although its retained caption leaves the revised aggregation unclear.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantive tests of initialization choice and dependence on task-level supervision (Tables 4 and 9). It also replaces the temporal gradient summary with an analysis of differences across layers (Figure 9). Existing bridge/freezing ablations, data-size sensitivity, cross-task transfer and task-description robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports benchmark run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both versions of Figure 9 contain shaded bands without defining their statistical meaning; v2 introduces no identifiable new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original matched LaMP scores are unchanged, but v2 adds initialization, data-access and LongLaMP results, explicit anchor-generation timings and revised gradient findings. For example, new Table 10 reports abstract-generation ROUGE-1/ROUGE-L of 0.2369/0.1643 for PRISP versus 0.1801/0.1236 for OPPU. These are newly reported results, not improvements over a corresponding v1 experiment.

T1.justification: New Appendix D derives trainable-parameter counts and their ratio, (d_out+r)/(d_in+d_out), alongside rank and fixed-subspace constraints for BCA and a restricted hypothesis class. V1 contains the method's matrix equations but lacks these complexity and subspace derivations. The robustness discussion is an argument rather than a statistical generalization proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: efficient task-data-free personalization, strong performance, privacy protection, unseen-task adaptability and task-description robustness. The additional evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the mechanistic account with structural-prior and bias–variance arguments. It replaces the generally stronger-gradient/faster-adaptation explanation with selective adaptation in deeper layers, attributes alternative initializers' weaknesses to SVD instability, and interprets matched-access results as evidence of baseline dependence on task supervision. The stated static-personalization and hypernetwork limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project code link, discloses training on both plain and BM25/profile-augmented examples, and explains inference prompt variants. It quantifies anchor generation as approximately 0.64 seconds for Qwen3-0.6B and 0.69 seconds for Llama-3.1-8B. Existing hardware, LoRA configuration, hyperparameters and hypernetwork pretraining details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Meng et al. (2024, PiSSA) and Wang et al. (2024, LoRA-GA), positioning semantic hypernetwork initialization against these alternatives. The existing related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged. LongLaMP was already cited in v1; bibliographic formatting updates do not represent additional research coverage.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. V2 expands the PRISP acronym, repeatedly replaces 'our method' with 'PRISP', adds acknowledgments and headings for the new material, and standardizes references. These are localized edits rather than extensive rewriting or narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 4, 9 and 10, redraws Figure 9 with layer index instead of training steps, and relocates retained displays. It also corrects boldface winner highlighting in the larger-model table (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 8). Figures 1–8 and the overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: The added data-access controls and LongLaMP tests broaden empirical support, while training details, measured latencies and a code link improve reproducibility. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Table 4's PRISP scores match retrieval-augmented entries in Table 13 despite Section 4.3's no-retrieval statement, and Figure 9 retains a caption describing averaging across layers at each training step despite now plotting layer index. The net improvement is useful but limited.
